answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils costly. A new agent earns trust only when established peers co-sign it and lock stake behind that vouch, like petals bound to a lotus. If a vouched identity cheats, each voucher bond is slashed, so endorsing a fake burns real capital. An attacker minting one hollow sonnet after another, each as disposable as cut quartz, must either buy vouches at market price or self-stake every identity, turning each extra sybil into linear, compounding cost.
